key_insight: Fine image detail does not necessarily require more global communication. SpecSlot separates globally shared image structure from locally modeled detail to reduce the attention burden of pixel-space generation.
problem_solved: Using one token per image patch makes finer-detail generation require more tokens, driving up the cost of global attention.
method: Introduce SpecSlot, a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer.
Use global exchange for low-frequency structure, such as broad shapes and layout.
Model high-frequency detail locally, aiming to decouple output detail from global token-sequence length.
impact: This approach could make detailed pixel-space image generation more computationally efficient. The supplied abstract is truncated and provides no quantitative results, so performance gains cannot be verified here.
visual_elements: Split image showing low-frequency shapes versus high-frequency edges and textures.
Side-by-side diagrams contrasting global attention over all patches with global structure exchange plus local detail modeling.
Conceptual cost diagram showing how adding globally attended tokens increases attention expense.
Global-network and local-magnifier icons to distinguish structure sharing from detail refinement.
paper_title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
paper_authors: Jiongfan Yang, Weichen Fan, Haiwen Diao, Zhongang Cai, Ziwei Liu
